headline: HEMLO HITS HIGH-GRADE: 16.1 g/t Gold Over 8.1 Metres in Newly Mapped South-Rim Zone at Ontario Mine
snippet: Hemlo Mining Corp. has intersected 16.1 g/t Au over 8.1 metres in a newly recognised South-Rim Zone sitting directly adjacent to active C-Zone production at its Ontario gold mine, part of a 130,000-metre 2026 exploration program. The high-grade intercept supports a newly mapped mineralised domain with potential for near-term, low-capital resource growth at one of Canada's historic gold camps.

headline: RIDGELINE BORES IN: South32's $4.4M Bet on Chinchilla CRD Silver-Zinc Discovery Kicks Off in Nevada
snippet: Ridgeline Minerals (TSXV: RDG) has kicked off three deep drill holes at its Chinchilla Sulfide carbonate replacement discovery within the Selena project in Nevada, funded by a South32 subsidiary under a Year-3 work program worth US$4.4 million. The holes will test manto-style CRD mineralisation between prior discovery holes and probe a new copper-silver skarn target, part of a record US$9.9M partner-funded 2026 exploration budget.

headline: EQUINOX SWALLOWS ORLA: $5.1 Billion Deal Creates $18.5B North American Senior Gold Producer
snippet: Equinox Gold is acquiring Orla Mining in a cash-and-stock deal valuing Orla at US$5.1 billion, with the combined entity reaching an US$18.5 billion market cap and targeting over one million gold ounces annually across six operating mines in Canada, the US, Mexico, and Nicaragua. The deal — backed by royalty industry legend Pierre Lassonde — is expected to close Q3 2026 pending shareholder votes in July, with CEO Darren Hall outlining an organic growth path to nearly two million ounces.

headline: COPPER ALARM: $14,000/Tonne Breached as African Mine Disruptions and China Demand Collide
snippet: LME copper surged above US$14,000 per tonne on May 13, approaching its January all-time high of $14,500, as sulfuric acid shortages caused by the US-Iran conflict disrupted African copper smelter output while Chinese industrial demand beat expectations. COMEX copper simultaneously hit a record $6.69/lb amid tariff-driven stockpiling, adding a premium of over $500/tonne above LME pricing.

headline: INDIA SLAMS THE DOOR: Bullion Import Tax More Than Doubles to 15% as Rupee Rout Bites
snippet: India raised import duties on gold and silver to 15% from 6% on May 13 — the largest single bullion tariff hike in years — as New Delhi races to defend the rupee and contain a current account deficit swollen by a 24% surge in gold imports to $71.98 billion in 2025-26. Analysts warn the move risks widening India's already-active smuggling networks and creating arbitrage pressure in the grey market.

headline: GOLD GIVES GROUND: 3.8% April CPI Crushes Fed Rate-Cut Bets, Sending Metal to $4,686
snippet: Gold slid to $4,686/oz after US April CPI came in at 3.8% — above the 3.7% forecast and the hottest reading since May 2023 — eliminating the residual 4.2% probability of a June Fed rate cut. The print extends gold's slide to 16% from its January all-time high of $5,589, with JPMorgan maintaining its $5,055/oz Q4 2026 target and framing the pullback as a structural buying window.

headline: RATIO ROUT: Gold-Silver Spread Crashes from 62 to 55 in One Week as Trade Truce Ignites Industrial Metal
snippet: The gold-to-silver ratio compressed from 62 to 54.94 in a single week after the US-China 90-day tariff reduction on May 10-11 triggered a 7.1% silver surge to $86.10/oz while gold barely moved, as traders repriced silver's industrial demand outlook — roughly 60% of annual silver goes to photovoltaics, EV components, and AI data centre buildout. With silver running a sixth consecutive annual supply deficit of 46.3 million ounces, the article explains the ratio-swap strategy sophisticated investors use to systematically accumulate ounces.

headline: RARE EARTH ULTIMATUM: China's Mineral Chokehold Heads the Agenda at Trump-Xi Beijing Summit
snippet: The Trump-Xi summit opening May 14 in Beijing is expected to pivot on China's control of 85-90% of global rare earth processing, which analysts say has become a more decisive lever than tariffs — a 10% supply disruption could trigger $150 billion in global economic losses within a year. The US-China rare earths deal struck in October remains nominally in force, but its extension is far from guaranteed.

headline: AMERICAN RARE EARTHS PUSH: Montana's Sheep Creek Project Taps Colorado Mines Tech to Build US Processing Chain
snippet: US Critical Materials Corp and Bayan Mining and Minerals have announced a collaboration to evaluate rare earth processing technologies at the Sheep Creek project in Montana, applying technology developed at Colorado School of Mines to build a US-based processing pathway aligned with national security and AI supply chain objectives. The deal is among a wave of Western critical mineral processing initiatives aimed at reducing dependence on Chinese rare earth refineries.

headline: WYOMING URANIUM CAMPAIGN BEGINS: Premier American Starts 100,000 ft ISR Drill Program at Kaycee, Powder River Basin
snippet: Premier American Uranium (TSXV: PUR) has commenced a 100,000-foot in-situ recovery exploration drill program at the Kaycee ISR Uranium Project in Wyoming's Powder River Basin, one of the most prolific uranium-producing regions in North America. The program follows a January 2026 resource expansion and targets further delineation of mineralisation as uranium demand from AI data centres and the nuclear energy buildout tightens the long-term supply outlook.

headline: BEYOND THE PULLBACK: Why JPMorgan and Major Banks Still Target $5,000 Gold Despite a 16% Correction
snippet: With gold down 16% from its January $5,589 all-time high, JPMorgan Global Research maintains a Q4 2026 average target of $5,055/oz on the basis of central bank demand averaging 585 tonnes per quarter and continued structural dollar-weakening dynamics. This analysis surveys why the largest institutional forecasters treat the current pullback as a mid-cycle retracement rather than the end of the bull run.
